headline: 10 dead in avalanche: Body of climber Nirmal Purja recovered from Broad Peak
summary: The renowned British-Nepali climber and nine team members were killed in a disaster on one of the world's highest peaks in northern Pakistan.
details: Rescuers have recovered the body of world-renowned climber Nirmal Purja after a devastating avalanche killed him and nine other team members.
The disaster occurred on Broad Peak, one of the world's highest peaks located in northern Pakistan.
The avalanche struck on Thursday, cutting off all contact with the international expedition led by the 43-year-old British-Nepali climber.
A ground rescue team located Purja's body at approximately 5,700 meters on the mountain.
According to the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the rescue team is transporting four bodies down from the mountain, including Purja, two other Nepali nationals, and a Chinese citizen.
Rescuers have also confirmed the presence of one additional body at a significantly higher elevation.

A ground rescue team located Purja's body at approximately 5,700 meters on the mountain.

According to the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the rescue team is transporting four bodies down from the mountain, including Purja, two other Nepali nationals, and a Chinese citizen.

Rescuers have also confirmed the presence of one additional body at a significantly higher elevation.

headline_marked: Legendary singer [[Runa Laila returns to Sydney stage]] after 10 years
headline: Legendary singer Runa Laila returns to Sydney stage after 10 years
summary: The iconic artist captivated nearly 2,000 expatriate Bangladeshis at the Northwest Convention Center during 'Bangladesh Night 2026'.
details: Legendary singer Runa Laila returned to the Sydney stage after a decade, performing for nearly 2,000 expatriate Bangladeshis at the Northwest Convention Center last Saturday.
Despite being 73, the artist displayed her signature vocal strength and emotion, performing a wide array of hits including the crowd-favorite 'Damadam Mast Kalandar'.
The event, titled 'Bangladesh Night 2026', was organized by 'Listen For' to celebrate its 10th anniversary, featuring a 25-member team of artists and technicians from Bangladesh.

The evening began with performances by Pintu Ghosh, followed by music director and artist Emon Chowdhury with the 'Bengal Symphony', as well as Aleya Begum, Mithun Chakravarty, and Erfan Mridha Shiblu.
A special highlight was the 'Sing with Laila' competition, where Runa Laila personally selected Elora Khan as the winner, who then performed 'Je Jon Premer Bhab Jane Na' alongside the legend.
To honor her six-decade musical journey, actress Naznin Niha presented a special award to Runa Laila during the event.
The venue also featured a memorial wall showcasing vinyl records, photographs, and memorabilia from Runa Laila's famous albums, drawing large crowds of fans.
Attendees described the event as a cultural festival rather than just a concert, praising the professional organization and the high international standard of the production.
caption:
After a 10-year wait, the legendary Runa Laila returned to Sydney, captivating 2,000 fans with her timeless voice.

Legendary singer Runa Laila returned to the Sydney stage after a decade, performing for nearly 2,000 expatriate Bangladeshis at the Northwest Convention Center last Saturday.

Despite being 73, the artist displayed her signature vocal strength and emotion, performing a wide array of hits including the crowd-favorite 'Damadam Mast Kalandar'.

The event, titled 'Bangladesh Night 2026', was organized by 'Listen For' to celebrate its 10th anniversary, featuring a 25-member team of artists and technicians from Bangladesh.

The evening began with performances by Pintu Ghosh, followed by music director and artist Emon Chowdhury with the 'Bengal Symphony', as well as Aleya Begum, Mithun Chakravarty, and Erfan Mridha Shiblu.

A special highlight was the 'Sing with Laila' competition, where Runa Laila personally selected Elora Khan as the winner, who then performed 'Je Jon Premer Bhab Jane Na' alongside the legend.

To honor her six-decade musical journey, actress Naznin Niha presented a special award to Runa Laila during the event.

The venue also featured a memorial wall showcasing vinyl records, photographs, and memorabilia from Runa Laila's famous albums, drawing large crowds of fans.

Attendees described the event as a cultural festival rather than just a concert, praising the professional organization and the high international standard of the production.
